And we want to maintain our status. All we care about is power. Fundamentally, humans are fundamentally imagination and we care about three things: the first is expressing our religion through art, music, and rituals; we want to know where we came from, why we're here, where we're going. That's who we really are. Second, we are diverse and want to differentiate ourselves by standing out, being different, and being creative. Third, we are curious and want to explore.

Throughout human history, this has been true. We may not have documents saying that we were traveling, but there were always some of us who wanted to go and see a new world, even if it didn't exist. That's who we are fundamentally. So don't believe people when they say you just care about money, power, or sex; we are fundamentally religious spiritual beings that want to create and to love and to connect.

Women could choose who to sleep with and how many men they slept with; often, they chose to sleep with everyone because it allowed them to create social cohesion. For early civilizations, women were the core and center of all societies.

There is a strategy in sleeping with many different men: now everyone is responsible for raising a child. If I am this father and know exactly who my children are, I will protect my children and discard everyone else. But if no one knows who the fathers are, everyone is responsible for caring for every single child, which ensures that every child becomes successful.

Humans follow the iron rule of nature, survival of the fittest, taught by Darwin. That's wrong; throughout most of human history, humans cared for each other and were compassionate and empathetic. We believe that every creature has divinity, and those who are weakest have the most divinity. When we kill an animal, we still thank it because we're all part of the same life cycle.

Humans have gotten smarter over the centuries; civilization is far superior to primitive cultures. This is wrong. The truth is that with the development of civilization, human imagination has decreased. Our brains can be supercomputers if we allow them to be. If people are more creative and have better memories, they recall more stuff, store more information, perceive more sensitively, empathize more, know exactly how you're feeling, why you're feeling it, and how to make you feel better; they have greater emotional resilience, which means they are much more mature than we are.

We evolve from apes. The truth is that we are uniquely imaginative and can choose our own evolution. Don't believe you're an ape. If you believe you're an ape, then you like to go beat people up and have sex with a lot of women; but we are not apes.
